name: grimmsnarl_ml_v17
policy: v16 exactly, with PRESERVE completed: when a dead-wall turn offers an evolution that would consume the last Impidimp or Morgrem, a free dead Shadow Bullet (or END) closes the turn instead, even when that basic body's current attack is too slow for BREAK's eight-turn gate.
one_change: wall_break.py only: complete the same wall-break route through strict last-breaker preservation and one residual Punk Up target

ranker.source: identical to grimmsnarl_ml_v8, v14, v15 and v16

evidence_base.identical_agents: the two submissions are byte-identical; they are pooled

v15_is_solved.claim: attack access is closed and is not the bottleneck any more
v15_is_solved.conclusion: every remaining late Shadow Bullet is a late Grimmsnarl ex, not an unreachable one

levers_measured_and_rejected.two_turn_boss_route: a playable Boss's Orders would have added a prize on 1 of 446 Shadow Bullets
levers_measured_and_rejected.bench_thirty_targeting: an offered lethal Bench-30 was passed over on 2 of 397 shots
levers_measured_and_rejected.adrena_brain_uptake: taken on 98.6% of the 346 turns it was offered, 100% in the losses
levers_measured_and_rejected.attacker_construction_gate: a Grimmsnarl-line play was passed over at END once in 176 no-attacker turns
levers_measured_and_rejected.mirror_live_unfair_stamp: Unfair Stamp was playable on 12 of our mirror turns and was played on all 12; opponents had 25 such turns and played all 25, so the usage gap is availability rather than refusal
levers_measured_and_rejected.note: these are offer-side, so no preference or planner change can move them; the two-turn prize planner and a mirror Stamp override were dropped on this evidence

wall_break.problem: 84 Shadow Bullets over the two runs were thrown while the opposing Active prevents all damage from us and the Bench-30 could take no prize either. The wall matchup is 7-8, 8.25 swings a game in the losses, 86.4% of them taking nothing, mean deck left 7.6, and two games ended in deck-out.
wall_break.mechanism: the three walls block different things, and none of them blocks Marnie's Morgrem: Crustle and Sylveon stop Pokemon ex, Cornerstone Mask Ogerpon ex stops Pokemon with an Ability, Neutralization Zone stops ex and V against a non-Rule-Box body. Morgrem is neither an ex nor an Ability holder, so Corkscrew Punch's 60 lands through all of them.
wall_break.why_only_two_breakers: Basic Darkness is the only Energy in the 60, and Frost Smash is {W}{C}, Mind Bend is {P}{C} and Chilly is {W}. Froslass, Munkidori and Snorunt can never attack at all, so a breaker is Morgrem for 60 or Impidimp for 10.
teeth: BREAK: while the swing is provably worth zero, advance the route to the breaker - attack with it, fuel it, or retreat into it - instead of throwing the swing
PRESERVE: do not spend the last breaker on a Grimmsnarl ex evolution while that wall is up and a fuelled Grimmsnarl ex is already in play
fires_only_when: the opposing Active takes 0 from Shadow Bullet and the Bench-30 takes no prize
no playable Boss's Orders would take a prize this turn (that route is already saturated, so it is left to the ranker)
for BREAK, a breaker in play knocks that Active out within 8 own turns and before our deck runs out
for BREAK, the breaker survives their best printed attack, or the wall has already proved permanent over two consecutive own turns
for PRESERVE, another fuelled Grimmsnarl ex already exists and a dead Shadow Bullet or END can close the turn without consuming the last Impidimp/Morgrem
for Punk Up, the triggering Grimmsnarl ex already has two Darkness and an offered Morgrem is still short of its second
wall_break.stickiness: the route is recomputed from the board every decision, exactly as attack_access does, so there is no plan to go stale; the only cross-decision state is the promotion serial and the consecutive dead-turn counter

measured_footprint.games_touched: the wall module is confined to the 15 wall games; v17 adds 7 guard-level differences across 5 of them and zero elsewhere

deliberately_not_done.forced_boss: 1 missed Boss prize in 446 swings; the guard stands down instead
deliberately_not_done.zero_damage_shadow_ban: banning it outright took a previous wall specialist to 1-10; both END and ATTACK close the turn, so the swing costs nothing on its own
deliberately_not_done.stall_circuit_breaker: the deck-out comes from the draw at the start of each turn, not from the swing, so refusing to attack saves no cards

v17_completion.problem: v16 reused BREAK's immediate eight-turn viability test for PRESERVE, so a last Impidimp whose current 10 damage was too slow could still be evolved away even though it was the only future Morgrem
v17_completion.strict_preserve_change: the six residual evolves become a dead Shadow Bullet; all six stored decisions offered both Shadow and END
v17_completion.punk_target_change: one split allocation now gives Morgrem its second Darkness instead of leaving both Morgrem and Impidimp at one
v17_completion.scope_probe: 7 differences over 9753 stored decisions: all 7 in wall games, zero in mirror, Alakazam, Festival and other matchups

policy_escalation.unchanged_from: grimmsnarl_ml_v6, except for the matchup gate below

v16_mirror_suspension.change: the class is not escalated when the public-information router reports a mirror; the pinned teacher answers instead
v16_mirror_suspension.problem: v6 escalated to reduce a 95.7% Froslass rate to 80.5%. Off the mirror the deployed agent takes it on 85.6% of offering turns, which is the intended target. On mirror boards it takes it on 30%, which no pilot in the corpus plays.
v16_mirror_suspension.honest_limit: this is an imitation gap, not an outcome gap: within our own 36 mirror games taking the evolve does not itself predict winning (4 of 15 offering turns in wins, 2 of 5 in losses). The argument is that a rate no teacher plays is not imitation, and the fallback is v5's behaviour on one matchup.
v16_mirror_suspension.information_used: opponent active, bench, discard, pre-evolutions and stadium only; no hidden hand or deck

residual.board_condition: the opponent took no prize during their last turn, and no Unfair Stamp is already in hand

wall_guard.interaction_with_wall_break: the wall guard swaps a zero-damage Shadow Bullet for one development action and then keeps quiet; wall_break runs after it and is what supplies a route once development is exhausted

router.role: public-information telemetry, and from v16 the mirror flag for the escalation gate

layer_order.why: attack_access requires the Shadow Bullet to be worth something and wall_break requires it to be worth nothing, so the two can never contend for the same board; ordering wall_break last is the direction that cannot lose a prize

files_changed_from_v16.main.py: version rationale only; runtime wiring is unchanged
files_changed_from_v16.wall_break.py: complete PRESERVE and route one residual Punk Up target

files_changed_from_v15.main.py: loads wall_break and sets the mirror flag from the router
files_changed_from_v15.ml_runtime.py: the escalation gate, plus its counter

promotion_gate.primary_kpi: rating drift over at least 50 games started from 1000+, not a peak
promotion_gate.regression_gate: first Shadow Bullet own turn <= 3.1 and Shadow by own turn 2 >= 0.35; v15's gains must not be given back
promotion_gate.wall_kpi: zero games lost by deck-out while a breaker was in play, and prizes per Shadow Bullet in the wall matchup above 0.212
promotion_gate.mirror_kpi: Froslass uptake when offered above 0.8, and mirror rating drift >= 0
promotion_gate.counterfactual: GRIMMSNARL_WALL_BREAK_DISABLE=1 with GRIMMSNARL_ESCALATION_MIRROR=on must reproduce v15 decision for decision
promotion_gate.attribution: the two changes fire on disjoint game sets - wall matchups and mirrors - so one run measures both

next_candidates_not_in_this_version: the mirror prize race after the first Shadow Bullet: we are faster (2.47 against 2.89) and take more prizes (3.81 against 2.56) and still go 21-15
the Festival/Dipplin matchup, 0-4 with a mean opponent rating of 1085 and only 0.5 Shadow Bullets a game
catastrophic losses to sub-800 opponents as a KPI of their own
closed-loop v17 ladder outcomes; the stored-board footprint proves scope and legality, not win rate
description: v16 completed rather than widened: preserve all eight stored last wall breakers instead of two, and finish the single Punk Up allocation that otherwise leaves an offered Morgrem one Darkness short. The seven additional stored-board decisions are all in wall games.
